title: DDQ templates: types and examples by industry
summary: A practical guide to DDQ templates: the main types, real example questionnaires by industry with sources, response templates you can download, and how to respond faster.
body_markdown:
A due diligence questionnaire looks different depending on who is asking and why. An investor vetting a fund, a bank screening a counterparty, and a buyer assessing a SaaS vendor all send a DDQ, but each asks about different things. Using the right DDQ template saves you from writing responses from scratch and makes sure you cover what the buyer expects.


This guide covers the main types of DDQ templates, real example questionnaires by industry with links to the recognized standards, response templates you can download, and how to respond to a DDQ faster. If you need the fundamentals first, start with our[DDQ meaning guide](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/ddq-meaning) ; this article stays focused on templates and examples.


## **The main types of DDQ templates**


Most DDQs fall into one of seven types. The template you choose should match the risk being assessed.


Type Who sends it What it assesses Recognized standard


Investment / fund DDQ Limited partners, allocators Strategy, team, terms, track record ILPA, AIMA


Operational due diligence (ODD) Institutional investors Operations, controls, service providers AIMA ODD


Vendor / third-party risk DDQ Procurement, risk teams Vendor risk, continuity, data handling Shared Assessments SIG


IT / security DDQ Security, IT buyers Security controls, certifications, data SIG, CAIQ


ESG DDQ Investors, procurement Environmental, social, governance practices UN PRI, Invest Europe


AML / KYC DDQ Banks, financial institutions Ownership, sanctions, financial crime controls Wolfsberg Group


M&A due diligence Acquirers, legal teams Financials, contracts, liabilities, IP Internal/legal

## **DDQ examples by industry**


You are usually on the receiving end of a DDQ: an investor sends one to your fund, a buyer sends one to your company, a bank sends one to your institution. Each industry has a recognized questionnaire, so you can see what you will be asked and prepare your answers in advance instead of scrambling each time.


For each context below, here is the standard DDQ, what it asks you to prove, and the response template to prepare your answers.


### **Private equity and venture capital**


If you manage a fund, limited partners will assess you with the[ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire](https://ilpa.org/resources-tools/resource-library/due-diligence-questionnaire/) , the model form from the Institutional Limited Partners Association. Expect to provide:


- Your track record across prior funds, including gross and net IRR and DPI.
- Your team structure and key-person provisions.
- Your fee structure, carried interest, and any offsets.


Prepare these responses once with our[private equity DDQ template](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/ddq-template-for-private-equity) .


### **Hedge funds**


If you manage a hedge fund, allocators will assess you with the[AIMA Due Diligence Questionnaires](https://www.aima.org/sound-practices/due-diligence-questionnaires.html) , the Alternative Investment Management Association's standard for investment managers and funds of funds. Expect to provide:


- Your strategy, the instruments you trade, and your typical leverage.
- Your service providers, prime broker, administrator, and auditor, and how often the fund is valued.
- Your risk management framework and position limits.


Prepare your DDQ responses with our[AIMA DDQ template](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/aima-ddq-template) .


### **Banking and financial services (AML / KYC)**


If you are a bank or financial institution, counterparties and correspondents will assess you with the[Wolfsberg Correspondent Banking DDQ (CBDDQ)](https://wolfsberg-group.org/resources/correspondent-banking) , the financial-crime standard from the Wolfsberg Group. Expect to prove:


- Your ultimate beneficial ownership and group structure.
- Your sanctions screening program and the lists you screen against.
- That your AML program is independently tested, and how often.


Prepare your responses with our[finance and banking DDQ template](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/ddq-template-finance-banking) , plus the downloadable AML/KYC response template in the section below.


### **IT, security, and vendor risk**


If you are a vendor, buyers will assess you with the[Shared Assessments SIG](https://sharedassessments.org/) (Standardized Information Gathering) questionnaire, the third-party risk standard covering security, continuity, and data handling. Expect to prove:


- The certifications you hold, such as SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001, and their dates.
- How you encrypt customer data at rest and in transit.
- Your incident response and breach notification process.


Prepare your responses with our[cybersecurity DDQ template](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/ddd-template-cyber-security) ,[IT infrastructure DDQ](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/it-infrastructure-ddq) , or[supplier risk assessment template](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/supplier-risk-assessment-template) .


### **ESG**


If investors or buyers assess your ESG practices, they will often use the[UN PRI Responsible Investment DDQs](https://public.unpri.org/investment-tools/asset-owner-resources/asset-owner-ddqs) , the Principles for Responsible Investment questionnaires for hedge funds and private markets. Expect to prove:


- Your ESG policy and who holds board-level accountability for it.
- How you measure and report greenhouse gas emissions and set targets.
- How you assess ESG risk in your supply chain or portfolio.

## **What a good DDQ response template includes**


Whatever the type, a strong DDQ response template shares the same backbone, so your prepared answers cover everything an assessor looks for. Check yours includes:


- **Company and ownership information.** Legal entity, structure, ownership, and key contacts.
- **The core risk area.** The heart of the questionnaire, whether that's investment strategy, security controls, or financial crime.
- **Governance and controls.** Your policies, oversight, and how you enforce them.
- **Third parties and service providers.** Who else is involved and how you manage them.
- **Compliance and certifications.** Relevant standards, audits, and evidence, with dates.
- **Supporting documents.** The attachments assessors expect, such as audited financials or a SOC 2 report.


## **How to respond to a DDQ**


When a DDQ lands, it can pull in several teams and take days. A repeatable process keeps each one faster and more consistent than the last.


- **Centralize your source answers.** Keep your approved answers, policies, certifications, and past DDQs in one place, so responders aren't hunting through inboxes and drives.
- **Map incoming questions to what you already have.** Most questions repeat across DDQs. Match each one to an existing approved answer before writing anything new.
- **Route only new or material questions to experts.** Send the genuinely new items to the right subject-matter expert, and reuse the standard answers.
- **Attach evidence and keep it current.** Support each answer with its source document, and check that certifications and figures are the latest version before you submit.
- **Review, then log the outcome.** Have a reviewer approve anything material, then save the final answers back to your library so the next DDQ starts further ahead.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are the main types of DDQ?


The most common are investment or fund DDQs, operational due diligence, vendor and third-party risk DDQs, IT and security DDQs, ESG DDQs, AML and KYC DDQs, and M&A due diligence. Each assesses a different kind of risk, so the template differs.


### Is there a standard DDQ template?


Several industries publish recognized standards you can start from: ILPA for private equity, AIMA for hedge funds, the Wolfsberg CBDDQ for correspondent banking, UN PRI for ESG, and Shared Assessments SIG for third-party and security risk. Most teams prepare their answers against one of these rather than starting from a blank page.


### What is the difference between a DDQ and a security questionnaire?


A security questionnaire is a specific type of DDQ that assesses only information security, such as certifications, encryption, and access controls. A broader DDQ also covers areas like financials, operations, ownership, and compliance.


### How do you respond to a DDQ faster?


Start from a response template that matches the relationship, reuse approved answers from past DDQs instead of rewriting them, and route only new or material answers to an expert for review. Response software automates most of that reuse.
